counterexample:
Witness: can_read("mallory", "alice", public=False). The frozen source body is `return public or bool(requester)`, which ignores `owner` entirely; with public=False and a nonempty requester the disjunction evaluates to True, so a non-owner authenticated requester is granted read access to a private document. The README rule permits access only for public documents or a requester equal to owner, so the owner-equality branch is never enforced.

Executed controls: the baseline probe imported the shipped module from the read-only source mount and called the real can_read, observing can_read_private_non_owner=true, can_read_private_owner=true, can_read_private_anonymous=false, can_read_public_anonymous=true (exit 0). These four observations are exactly the truth table of `public or bool(requester)` and are inconsistent with any owner-checking policy, so the observation is bound to the shipped implementation rather than to the harness. The counterexample run executed the identical four probe inputs against a README-conformant reference policy (public -> allow; else requester and requester == owner) and flipped only the decisive cell to can_read_private_non_owner=false, yielding claim_present=false (exit 0), while still loading the shipped symbol and reporting its signature ["requester","owner","public"].

Assessment of the controls: the pair is a genuine differential — the only variable changed between runs is the policy implementation on fixed inputs, and the harness demonstrably reports false when the implementation conforms, so the baseline's true is not print-only, hard-coded, or argv-echoed. Weakness noted: the negation arm's decisive computation is an in-probe reference policy rather than a mutated copy of the source, so it establishes harness sensitivity rather than a source-derived negation; the source-bound half of the distinction rests on the baseline alone. That baseline is nonetheless a direct call into the frozen file whose outputs uniquely match the frozen source text, which is sufficient for a meaningful executed distinction.
